steps.text: Hi team. We need a product plan for Streakly, our habit-tracking app, for the board meeting in three weeks. @pm please get the research started first; I want the plan grounded in what competitors actually do.

steps.reply: I sized the market and compared the five strongest competitors. The clear gap is what happens after a missed day: every app punishes it and loses the user. Submitting the analysis.

args.summary: Market size, five competitors compared, the missed-day gap and price points
args.content:
Market analysis: habit tracking apps (2026).

Size: about 38 million people in the US and EU used a habit or routine app in the last year; roughly 6% pay. Consumer spending is around USD 410 million a year and grows about 9% a year, mostly through subscriptions.

Competitors: Habitica (gamified, strong community, dated design), Streaks (iOS only, very polished, one-time price), Loop (free and open source, Android only), Fabulous (coaching content, expensive at USD 39.99 a year) and Way of Life (simple charts, weak reminders).

Gap: none of them handles a missed day well. Users who break a long streak churn within a week in every app we reviewed. A forgiving streak (one free skip per week, and a recovery flow) is the clearest gap we can own.

Price points: free tiers limit habits to 3-5; paid tiers sit between USD 2.99 and 4.99 a month.

steps.notes: Clear and well sourced. The missed-day gap is a strong angle; keep the price points handy for pricing.

steps.reply: Starting on the feature set. Before I design the recovery flow I want to know whether any competitor already has a shared or team streak. @research can you check?

args.text: @research does any competitor offer a shared or team streak, and how do users react to it?
Recovery flow: start from the morning-after notification; check competitor team mechanics before designing.

steps.reply: @ux Habitica is the only one with a shared mechanic: parties lose health when one member misses a daily. Users like the accountability but say it feels punishing; about a third of party members we read about left after a single bad week. Nobody offers a team streak with a tolerance threshold, so there is room for a forgiving version.

args.text: Habitica is the only one with a shared mechanic: parties lose health when one member misses a daily. Users like the accountability but say it feels punishing; about a third of party members we read about left after a single bad week. Nobody offers a team streak with a tolerance threshold, so there is room for a forgiving version.

steps.reply: Drafted a freemium consumer model based on the competitor price points: free up to 4 habits, Plus at USD 3.99 a month.

args.summary: Freemium consumer pricing with conversion and revenue at 50,000 users
args.content:
Consumer pricing proposal.

Model: freemium. Free plan with up to 4 habits and the basic streak; Plus at USD 3.99 a month or USD 29.99 a year with unlimited habits, the forgiving streak, reminders by location and the yearly report.

Conversion: the category converts 4-7% of active users; we assume 5%. At 50,000 monthly active users that is 2,500 paying users and about USD 95,000 a year after store fees.

Risks: a one-time price like Streaks would undercut us on iOS; the forgiving streak must be clearly a Plus feature to justify the price.

steps.reply: Here is the first version of the MVP feature set with the onboarding, check-in and recovery flows. Thanks @research for the note on Habitica parties.

args.summary: MVP feature set v1 with onboarding, check-in, forgiving streak and recovery flows
args.content:
MVP feature set v1.

1. Onboarding: pick up to three habits from templates, set a reminder time. 2. Daily check-in from a widget or a notification, one tap per habit. 3. Streak view with a calendar. 4. Forgiving streak: one free skip per week, applied automatically. 5. Streak recovery: after a miss, a three-day comeback challenge restores half of the old streak. 6. Weekly summary notification on Sunday evening.

User flows: onboarding takes under a minute; the check-in flow has no extra screens; the recovery flow starts from the notification sent the morning after a miss.

Later: social sharing, Apple Health import, coaching content.

steps.notes: Good flows, but there is no way to tell whether any feature works: none of them has a success metric, so we cannot cut scope later on evidence. Please add one metric per feature.
conventions: Every feature in the plan names the metric that shows it works.

steps.text: Change of requirements after talking to investors: we will sell Streakly to small teams instead of individual consumers. Pricing has to be per seat, and the buyers are managers who will ask about SSO and data privacy. The consumer pricing work can stop.

steps.reply: Switched to per-seat pricing. I am including SSO in every plan, since team buyers treat it as a basic requirement.

args.text: SSO and the audit log are included in every plan, not sold as an add-on.
args.rationale: Team buyers expect them, and charging extra would push us above competitors at the low end.
rejected: SSO as a USD 2 per seat add-on

args.summary: USD 4 per seat per month, USD 40 per year, minimum 5 seats, revenue at 300 teams
args.content:
Per-seat pricing for teams.

Price: USD 4 per seat per month billed monthly, or USD 40 per seat per year (two months free). Minimum 5 seats. 14-day free trial with no card. SSO and the audit log are included in every plan, because team buyers expect them and competitors charge extra for them.

Revenue: at 300 paying teams with an average of 18 seats, and 70% on annual billing, the annual revenue is about USD 247,000.

Comparison: workplace wellbeing tools charge USD 3-8 per seat; our price sits at the low end, which keeps the pilot decision under most managers' approval limit.

steps.reply: Collected what team buyers ask for before signing, plus one privacy rule from interviews that affects the dashboard design.

args.summary: SSO, GDPR terms, EU residency, export and audit log now; SOC 2 later; aggregate-only dashboard
args.content:
Security and compliance requirements for team buyers.

Must have in the first release: SAML and OIDC single sign-on; a GDPR data processing agreement and EU data residency (hosting in Frankfurt); an export of all of a team's data as CSV; an admin audit log of invites, removals and role changes kept for one year; encryption at rest and in transit.

Can wait: SOC 2 Type II (start the audit window at launch, report after six months); SCIM user provisioning; customer-managed keys.

Privacy rule from interviews: employees will not join if managers can see who missed a day. The dashboard must only show aggregate participation.

steps.notes: Pricing is clear and the revenue estimate states its assumptions. Including SSO is the right call.

steps.reply: Reworked the feature set for teams and added a success metric to every feature, as the new convention asks. The dashboard only shows aggregates, following the compliance note.

args.summary: MVP feature set v2 for teams, with a metric per feature
args.content:
MVP feature set v2 (teams).

1. Team setup: an admin invites people by email or SSO and picks up to five shared team habits. Metric: 70% of invited people check in within three days. 2. Daily check-in from a widget, Slack or a notification. Metric: median check-in under 10 seconds. 3. Personal streak with the forgiving skip. Metric: week-4 retention above 40%. 4. Team streak: the team keeps its streak while 80% of members check in. Metric: teams with a live team streak renew at twice the base rate. 5. Manager dashboard with participation by week, refreshed every five minutes, never showing individual misses. Metric: managers open it at least weekly. 6. Streak recovery flow, as in v1. Metric: 30% of broken streaks recovered.

Later: Apple Health import, coaching content, real-time dashboard.

steps.notes: Every feature now has a metric and the team streak threshold is a nice answer to the Habitica problem. Approved.
Complete and prioritised. The aggregate-only rule is now reflected in the feature set.

steps.text: @eng the first release has to fit in 10 engineer-weeks. If something does not fit, tell me what you would cut.

steps.reply: Reading the feature set and the compliance list. The dashboard refresh rate decides whether we need a realtime service, so I am checking with @ux.

args.text: @ux does the manager dashboard need realtime updates, or is a refresh every few minutes good enough?

steps.reply: @eng a refresh every five minutes is fine. Managers look at weekly participation, not live check-ins. I will note it in the feature list.

args.text: A five-minute refresh is fine; managers look at weekly participation, not live check-ins.

steps.reply: With a five-minute refresh the dashboard can read hourly rollups. A realtime version did not fit the budget, so I recorded that. Submitting the architecture and the estimate: 10 engineer-weeks.

args.text: A realtime websocket service for the manager dashboard.
args.reason: It adds about 2.5 engineer-weeks and pushes the release past the 10-week budget; a five-minute refresh meets the need.

args.summary: React Native + TypeScript API in the EU, 10 engineer-weeks with two engineers
args.content:
Architecture and delivery estimate.

Architecture: React Native app for iOS and Android sharing one codebase; a TypeScript API on a managed Postgres in the EU (Frankfurt); a Slack app for check-ins; SSO through a hosted identity provider rather than our own SAML code. The manager dashboard reads hourly rollups and refreshes every five minutes, so no websocket service is needed.

Estimate: mobile app 4 engineer-weeks, API and data model 2, SSO and audit log 1.5, Slack check-in 1, dashboard 1, hardening and store release 0.5. Total 10 engineer-weeks with two engineers, about five calendar weeks.

Risks: App Store review time for the first release; SSO edge cases with older Active Directory setups; widget refresh limits on iOS.

steps.notes: The estimate fits the 10-week budget and the risks are realistic. Approved.

steps.text: This is looking good. For the board meeting I need everything on a single page that I can read out in two minutes.

args.summary: One-page plan: problem, customer, product, price, delivery, risks
args.content:
Streakly for teams: one-page plan.

Problem: habit apps lose people the day they miss a streak, and nothing helps teams build habits together without shaming people.

Customer: teams of 5 to 200 people whose managers run wellbeing or learning programmes.

Product: shared team streaks with a tolerance threshold, a forgiving personal streak, check-in from Slack or a widget, and a manager dashboard that only shows aggregate participation.

Price: USD 4 per seat per month or USD 40 per seat per year; SSO and the audit log included. About USD 247,000 a year at 300 teams.

Delivery: 10 engineer-weeks with two engineers; EU hosting; SOC 2 audit window starts at launch.

Risks: app store review time, SSO edge cases, and whether teams keep the habit after the first month.

steps.notes: Reads well in two minutes and the numbers match the approved deliverables.
